title: observability-token-kv-cost-latency-tracing-dashboard-alert-tuning-extended
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Improve token-level observability for KV-backed workloads by extending dashboards, adding finer-grained metrics and spans, and tuning alert thresholds based on recent production traffic patterns. This change addresses recurring confusion during incidents where token cache behavior and per-token cost spikes were not visible at the right granularity.

Summary of changes: added new token-level KV metrics (token.kv.cache_hits, token.kv.cache_misses, token.kv.kv_lookup_latency_ms) and enhanced existing token cost/latency histograms with tags for model, route, customer_tier and sequence_length_bucket. Introduced tracing tag propagation for KV operations to correlate spans with token-level metrics. Built a new Grafana dashboard for token-kv cost/latency + traces, updated Prometheus recording rules and alerting policies to reduce noisy alerts by using adaptive baselines. Updated docs and e2e tests.

Checklist: - [x] Add metrics instrumentation and recording rules - [x] Add tracing context to KV paths - [x] Create Grafana dashboard + panels for cost/latency breakdowns - [x] Update alerting policies and tune thresholds - [x] Add unit and e2e tests - [x] Run rollout in staging and monitor alerts for one week

Rollout plan: deploy metric and tracing changes with a canary (10% traffic) for 48h, validate dashboards and alert behavior in staging, then full rollout. Alert changes will be staged as "notify-dev" for 72h before enabling pager escalation. We will monitor token_cost anomaly rates and revert thresholds if false positives exceed 0.5% of incidents.

Impact: improves troubleshooting speed by surfacing token-level KV interactions and per-token cost attribution, reduces pager noise via adaptive alerting, and provides SREs/product engineers with clearer cost/latency tradeoffs for batching and caching optimizations.
commits: feat(observability): add token.kv cache metrics and latency histogram
perf(tracing): propagate kv operation ids and add span tags for token metadata
chore(alerts): add recording rules and adaptive baseline alerts for token_cost and kv_latency
docs(observability): document new dashboard panels and interpretation guide
test(e2e): add observability smoke tests for token-kv metrics and alerts
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice incremental approach — can you clarify cardinality limits for the new token tags? We should cap sequence_length_bucket and ensure model tags are limited to a curated list.
Priya Shah (author): We added a sanitize step in token_metric_tags.toml and a cardinality gate in token_metrics_collector.go; the doc includes the curated model whitelist.
Maya Lin: Alert tuning looks reasonable but request lowering the sensitivity on the token_cost anomaly rule for low-traffic customers to avoid noisy p99 alerts.
Priya Shah (author): Adjusted the alert to use traffic_weighted_baseline and added an exclusion for customers with < 1k tokens/minute. Added tests to assert behavior.
Jordan Patel: Can you add an explicit note in the playbook about how to use trace links from the dashboard to span lookup? Also request a short smoke test that runs in CI.
Priya Shah (author): Added playbook section and e2e smoke test. CI job added to run observability smoke tests on merge.
release_notes: Added token-level KV metrics, new Grafana dashboard for token cost/latency, tracing propagation for KV spans, and tuned alerts to reduce noise. Recommended action: teams using custom dashboards should re-import the new token_kv_cost_latency dashboard and review alert thresholds for low-traffic customers.
notes_for_sre: Monitor the new recording rules for cardinality growth for the first 72h. If Prometheus scrape cardinality increases > 5% use the cardinality gate to roll back. Alert staging will be 'notify-dev' for 72h before pager escalation.
user_impact: No functional API changes. Observability-only changes; small CPU overhead (~1-2%) observed in staging due to additional metrics, compensated by sampling and cardinality gates.
